# Membership evidence batch 02 — historical revision

[中文](README.zh-CN.md) | **English**


WorkBuddy agent (AI), 24 October 2026, 22:20–23:05 Beijing time. This batch corrected batch01 and added evidence leads. It adopted zero production rules and did not modify production data, existing batches or Q1 outputs.

A full UPI report dated 3 July 1992 described admission of 14 associations, naming 12, and postponement of seven applications to a December Executive Committee meeting. It supplied proposals for six previously uncovered tasks. Linking that seven-country group to the 1994 report remained an inference, not a country-by-country FIFA decision.

The batch still supplied no newly acquired primary FIFA membership decision. The 2018 report was reused. News articles read online but not saved locally were not assigned fictitious local files or hashes. Provisional status, readmission and Congress approval still required separate interpretation.

The [batch review](../../../../../outputs/logs/team_identity/batch-review-20261024-batch02/README.en.md) verified 42 nonempty proposals, 30 task keys, 27 source teams and 298 distinct proposed matches. Task states were 26 partial, three conflict, one not_found and 118 not_reviewed. Source hashes and the unchanged batch01 were checked.

Remaining objections included overclaiming a 1994 decision, treating pre-approval as automatically non-member, unregistered conflicting dates, planned admission mistaken for completed admission, and correction records that bundled multiple old IDs. Coverage of match IDs did not establish verified eligibility.

The original evidence, coverage and correction records retain the detailed proposals and limitations. No production reconstruction, full pytest or independent new retrieval of the online UPI text was performed by the reviewer. These are dated collection records; use the [adopted identity guide](../../../../../研究/00_数据再次确认/README.en.md) for current scope.

Original preserved file: [README.md](README.md). This reading edition does not replace its registered evidence.
